points.text: Unclear whether missing frames are temporally aligned in occlusion simulation; validity unclear.
No justification for not using attention-based fusion.
Two-pass inference may double latency, limiting real-time use.
Gains may stem from pretrained Auto-AVSR rather than architecture.
Performance gain marginal relative to threefold parameters over IIANet.
Roles of coarse and fine stages unanalysed; may equal training twice as long.
Novelty limited; just adds an extra stage.
Coarse-to-fine not novel; A-FRCNN, CTCNet already iterative.
High computational cost; size and memory over 3x IIANet.
SP fusion similar to CTCNet and RTFS-Net approaches; should cite them.
SP fusion not compared with prior fusion methods.
Figure 5 hard to read.
RTFS-Net results missing from Table 1.
Table ordering confusing; best results not bolded.
Unclear if gains come from Auto-AVSR encoder or architecture; need encoder swap.
Table 2 unclear whether coarse-only or coarse+fine; coarse-only cost missing.
Gain not attributed: no no-video two-pass, non-AVSR encoder or matched-epoch controls.
Table 2 cost reflects single pass; efficiency trade-off unsupported.
Table 2 compares dynamic-mixing CSFNet to non-DM baselines.
Overclaims: necessity, robustness, best across all metrics.
10% WER reduction not reproducible from Table 5.
Table 3 baselines copied, variant unspecified, weak; implausible PESQ jump.
LRS3 DM coarse below non-DM; fine-gain variation unexplained.
No seeds or confidence intervals.
Suspicious timing values in Tables 2 and 6.
Single qualitative example; selection protocol unstated.
Undefined 'MAVINet'; 2-4 vs 2-5 speakers inconsistency.
Table 5 recogniser and reference WERs unstated; separation claim lacks SI-SDRi.
Novelty incremental; iterative/multi-stage separation work not discussed.
No cascade baseline without AVSR to support 'new paradigm'.
RTFS-Net omitted from comparison tables.
Noisy comparison uses older copied baselines; protocols mixed.
Citation errors affecting positioning.
Speaker-aware semantic representation claim lacks representation-level evidence.
Thin ML insight: no analysis why second pass helps; small deltas.
Indispensability of fine stage rests on one spectrogram example.
Experimental narrative overreaches; robustness and best-results claims.
Presentation inconsistencies: MAVINet, speaker counts, terminology, SP description.
No limitations section; conclusion repeats abstract.
Table header, equation and spelling typos.
No code statement.
Only synthetic mixtures without reverberation or real recordings.
Streaming/causal latency and on-device cost not reported.
Assumes tracked face crops and known speaker count.
Visual degradation simulated only as dropped frame blocks.
SP designed for 2 speakers but evaluated up to 5.
No broader impact, privacy, consent or demographic discussion.
Ignores joint separation-recognition and generative refiner literatures.
Gain not isolated from extra training, generic two-pass, or extra encoder.
Efficiency numbers count only one pass; pretrained encoders excluded.
DM fine result compared to non-DM baselines.
Table 6 confounds multi-range and hidden size; stage unstated.
SP compared only with concatenation, not attention fusion.
Baseline provenance unmarked; Table 3 omits strong AV methods; PESQ jump.
RTFS-Net absent from Table 1.
Possible Auto-AVSR overlap with test utterances not stated.
No variance; 0.2 dB coarse margin within noise.
Reproducibility: no code, freezing unstated, SP for N speakers undefined.
10% WER reduction headline not matching Table 5.
MAVINet undefined; speaker-count and gain-reporting inconsistencies.
Header and equation typos; timing artifacts.

P.summary: SP fusion not justified or compared against attention-based fusion.
High computational cost and poor cost-performance trade-off.
Gains may come from pretrained Auto-AVSR, not architecture.
SP fusion similar to prior work; citations missing.

Q.summary: Gain not isolated from extra training, generic two-pass, or AVSR encoder.
Efficiency cost counts only one pass.
DM vs non-DM mismatch in comparison.
Incremental novelty; iterative/refiner prior work undiscussed.
No representation-level analysis of why refinement helps.
SP designed for two speakers, used for more.
SP not compared with attention fusion.
